text: Every word or token that you feed into an AI starts out as a row of numbers called an
embedding.
As the AI processes your message, its internal layers perform calculations that constantly
alter those numbers to reflect the context of your prompt.
But as those numbers change, they stop matching the starting numbers for any known token.
So how can they still represent meaning?
An exact match isn't necessary.
The relationships between the numbers matter too.
We can picture those relationships as positions on a map, where nearby positions can represent
similar meanings.
That's the idea behind vector space.
This is a map using two numbers to describe position, latitude and longitude.
Dallas, Texas is at 33 degrees north, 97 degrees west.
Mountain View is at 37 degrees north, 122 degrees west.
And New York City is at 41 degrees north, 74 degrees west.
Now imagine you are handed two completely new sets of coordinates.
The first is 38 degrees north, 120 degrees west.
The second is 40 degrees north, 76 degrees west.
For each position, which of the three cities is closest?
The position 38 degrees north, 120 degrees west is closest to Mountain View.
The position 40 degrees north, 76 degrees west is closest to New York City.
When nothing matches exactly, distance finds the closest one.
Even though those new coordinates don't perfectly match any of our cities,
the relative position still tells us something concrete.
It tells us which city they are near.
Look at this table of Coke, Pepsi, and coffee.
Each is rated across seven characteristics, from sweet to citrus,
creating a row of numbers called a vector.
Coke and Pepsi's vectors are nearly identical.
Coffee's differ completely.
These seven ratings position each drink in a seven-dimensional vector space.
Plotting vectors creates spatial neighborhoods.
Coke and Pepsi sit close together.
Coffee is far away.
Look at their exact locations.
Physical gaps perfectly measure these numerical differences.
Now, suppose you are given the ratings for a mystery drink.
The numbers are 9, 1, 10, 2, 3, 8, 9.
Take a moment and guess which of our three established drinks is the closest match.
The mystery drinks ratings are closest to Pepsi's.
Its first six scores match perfectly.
Only the citrus column differs, a 9 instead of a 10,
leaving a gap of just one.
Compared with Coke, the citrus gap is 8.
That math drops the mystery drink right next to Pepsi.
Smaller gaps mean closer positions.
AI systems take this exact mathematical concept and scale it up to thousands of
dimensions to measure the distance between complex concepts.
Let's see how this physical movement maps meaning in actual language with a sentence.
The cat sat on the mat during the May rainstorm because it was tired.
On its own, the pronoun it is completely ambiguous.
At the beginning, it is a neutral token at an isolated starting position outside
the main neighborhoods, with baseline numbers like 0.12 and negative 0.34.
As layers extract context, calculations update the numbers,
moving the word through vector space.
It lands at coordinate 0.41, 0.06, reflecting its connection to cat.
Meaning is a position in vector space.
Similar meanings usually sit close together.
